what_its_for: Dimethyl fumarate is used to treat relapsing forms of multiple sclerosis (MS) in adults, including relapsing-remitting MS. It helps reduce the number of MS flare-ups (relapses) and can slow the buildup of disability. Skilarence is also approved to treat moderate to severe plaque psoriasis in adults.
how_to_take: Swallow the capsule or tablet whole. Do NOT crush, chew, or open it. Take it with food to help reduce stomach upset. Try to take it at the same times each day to help you remember. Taking it with a low-fat snack or meal is especially important if you experience stomach or flushing side effects.
dosing: For multiple sclerosis (Tecfidera): You will usually start on a lower dose of 120 mg twice daily for the first 7 days, then your doctor will increase your dose to 240 mg twice daily. For psoriasis (Skilarence): Dosing is gradually increased over several weeks, starting with 30 mg once daily and increasing as directed by your doctor. Always follow your doctor's specific instructions, as your dose may be adjusted based on how well you tolerate the medicine.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember — BUT only if your next scheduled dose is more than 4 hours away. If it is less than 4 hours until your next dose, skip the missed dose and take the next one at your regular time. Do NOT take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one.
storage: Store at room temperature between 59°F and 77°F (15°C to 25°C). Keep the bottle tightly closed. Protect from moisture and heat. Do not store in the bathroom. Keep this medicine out of reach of children and pets. Throw away any unused medicine after the expiration date on the label.
what_to_avoid: Avoid taking other medicines that lower your immune system without talking to your doctor first. Avoid grapefruit products unless your doctor says it is okay. Do not drink alcohol excessively, as it may worsen side effects. Let your doctor know before starting any new prescription or over-the-counter medications, vitamins, or herbal supplements. Avoid live vaccines while on this medication without checking with your doctor first.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or seek emergency help if you experience: signs of a serious infection such as fever, chills, or persistent cough; unusual weakness or tiredness; signs of a rare but serious brain infection called PML (progressive multifocal leukoencephalopathy) — symptoms include new or worsening weakness on one side of the body, vision changes, confusion, memory problems, or difficulty speaking; severe stomach pain or vomiting; signs of an allergic reaction such as hives, swelling of the face or throat, or difficulty breathing; significant decrease in white blood cell counts found on your blood tests; or yellowing of your skin or eyes.
when_it_works: It may take several months before you notice the full benefit of dimethyl fumarate. Some people see improvements within the first few months, but MS treatment is long-term. Your doctor will monitor your progress with regular MRI scans and blood tests (especially to check your white blood cell count). Do not stop taking this medicine without talking to your doctor, even if you feel well.
special_populations: Pregnancy and breastfeeding: Tell your doctor right away if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding. The safety of dimethyl fumarate during pregnancy is not fully established. Effective contraception is recommended during treatment. Elderly patients: Use with caution; your doctor may monitor you more closely. Kidney or liver problems: Tell your doctor if you have kidney or liver disease, as dose adjustments or extra monitoring may be needed. Children: Dimethyl fumarate is not approved for use in children under 18 years of age.
